title: Lettre Tate (mai 66) (Cristaux) : lettre (1966), tapuscrit (s.d.), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page continues §1.16 of Grothendieck's May 1966 letter to Tate on crystals. It is the birth of the infinitesimal (nilpotent, no divided powers) crystalline site.

(1) The site. The 'site cristallogène' of S/R has as objects R-morphisms U→T. Here U is an open of S and U→T is a surjective closed immersion defined by a nilpotent ideal. The topology is Zariski on T.
- A sheaf on this site is the same as a family of Zariski sheaves F_{U→T} on each T, together with transition maps from the pullbacks of F_{U'→T'} to F_{U→T}. These transition maps need not be isomorphisms; the manuscript adds that they are isomorphisms for open immersions.
- Taking O_T on each T gives the structure sheaf of rings O_C.

(2) Crystals as modules. Grothendieck claims that crystals of quasi-coherent modules on S/R are exactly the quasi-coherent O_C-modules, meaning modules locally the cokernel of a map of free modules. Crystals of finite presentation correspond to O_C-modules of finite presentation. This is the standard statement: for a quasi-coherent module on this ringed site, the transition maps are automatically isomorphisms.

(3) Functoriality. An R-morphism S'→S does not induce a morphism of sites. It does induce a morphism of topoi Topcr_{S'/R}→Topcr_{S/R}, built from the inverse-image construction of 1.3. This is the now-standard fact that the crystalline/infinitesimal topos is functorial although the site is not. Grothendieck flags that the inverse image needs care.

(4) The key test (§1.17). Take R the spectrum of a field and S smooth over R (and proper if char p>0). Then H^*(site, O_C) should be the de Rham cohomology of S/R.
- Relative version: for f:S'→S proper and smooth, the 'value on S'' of R^i f_{cris*}(O_{C'}) should be R^i f_*(Ω^•_{S'/S}).
- The Gauss–Manin connection should come from the crystal stratification of 1.8.
- Evidence offered: Grothendieck's own check that a Gauss–Manin connection exists for any smooth morphism, and the Washnitzer–Monsky theory.

(5) Later marginal correction. A handwritten note says 'marche en car. 0, et pas en car p>0 (faute d'introduire les puiss. div.)'. That is: this site works in characteristic 0 (infinitesimal cohomology = de Rham) but fails in characteristic p for lack of divided powers. That is exactly what led to Berthelot's PD-crystalline site.
errors: As stated (nilpotent thickenings without divided powers), the char p>0 part of the key test fails, even for S smooth and proper. Infinitesimal cohomology of O in char p does not compute de Rham cohomology. The marginal annotation itself corrects this.
The relative claim 'sans condition sur R' about R^i f_cris*(O_C') is likewise false for this site over bases of positive or mixed characteristic. Divided-power structures are needed.
Functoriality of the topos is asserted via the method of 1.3, but the author admits the inverse image is not carefully defined. This is a gap, later filled in the literature (SGA-style/Berthelot).

deep.surprise_reason: This is the well-known letter to Tate, whose content is widely cited as the origin of crystals. The infinitesimal site, its functoriality, the de Rham comparison and the later divided-powers correction are all documented in the literature. The only small extra is the handwritten later annotation, which merely records a known historical correction.
transcription_corrections: Margin note reads roughly: 'marche en car. 0, et pas en car p>0 (faute d'introduire les puiss. div.)'. The machine reading 'intro-duire[?]' is consistent with this.
The handwritten insertion above 'image inverse de faisceaux"' appears to read 'au sens inverse' (uncertain).
'Washnitzer-Monsky' is Grothendieck's typo for Washnitzer–Monsky (Monsky–Washnitzer); keep as in the original.
